summary: On the CAW transport (32 nodes), when one node removes and recreates a shared directory (the board's fence_during_write setup: rank 1 recreates /mnt/shared/.fence_during_write between rows/runs) a third of the peers get ESTALE from mkdir under it — for BOTH the child and the parent path — for at least the next ~0.5 s, i.e. their cached dentry/inode of the previous incarnation of that directory is served after the directory was unlinked and re-created cluster-wide. A retry 0.5 s later succeeds. Any application creating under a directory another node just recreated sees a spurious ESTALE (POSIX single-node semantics never produce it here). Data-integrity impact unknown (the retry succeeded; the same run's node16 also failed 'still writable' once).
